answer: Sealed-Question Identity Gate. Each agent must answer a fresh, randomly generated constraint-satisfaction puzzle whose solution forms a unique pigment-like fingerprint; the puzzle is drawn from a canyon of combinatorially distinct instances, so no answer repeats. A per-attack cost arises because each identity must solve one instance: fabrication scales linearly with compute, not free. Validity is checked by a single pulse of verification, then discarded, preventing replay. An attacker pays one compute-bound solve per fake identity, making mass sybils uneconomic.
